name: Tabaru
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_quote: This new syllable, however, has not affected the position of stress. Thus, in words which used to have a final consonant, stress falls on the antepenultimate syllable, since Tabaru tends to place the stress on the penultimate syllable of words without an echo-vowel. (Fortgens 1928)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Sources: the classification rests on Kotynski 1988 (held, quotes verified verbatim at pp.156/158/164) and is independently confirmed by Fortgens 1928 (downloaded now, p.329 and p.392). These are the only two descriptions of Tabaru stress in existence per Glottolog; nothing better is missing. The record's 'quote'/'cite'/'loc'/'grade' slots are empty even though sources[0] carries the verified Kotynski text — fill them (Kotynski 1988:156,158,164; Fortgens 1928:329,392) and set the grade accordingly. One coding caveat to keep visible rather than a reclassify: 'fixed-strict' penult is true only under the record's stated domain convention (echo vowel not counted: Fortgens 'rekent niet mede'; Kotynski underlying /odom/ with post-stress epenthesis).
